what_its_for: Zileuton is used to prevent and treat asthma in adults and children 12 years and older. It helps reduce swelling and tightening in your airways, making it easier to breathe. It is a long-term controller medicine and will NOT stop an asthma attack that has already started.
how_to_take: Take zileuton by mouth with or without food. Swallow the extended-release tablets (Zyflo CR) whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. The regular tablets (Zyflo) can be taken with or without food. Take this medicine every day as directed, even when you feel well. Always keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler (like albuterol) nearby for sudden asthma symptoms.
dosing: Regular tablets (Zyflo): The usual dose is 600 mg taken 4 times a day (with meals and at bedtime). Extended-release tablets (Zyflo CR): The usual dose is 1200 mg taken twice a day, within 1 hour after your morning and evening meals. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your needs. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store zileuton at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in a dry place such as a medicine cabinet — avoid storing in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking zileuton, as it can increase the risk of liver problems and worsen side effects. Do not take zileuton with certain medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first — especially warfarin (a blood thinner), theophylline (another asthma medicine), or propranolol (a beta-blocker). Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor. Do not use zileuton as your only treatment during a sudden asthma attack.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe tiredness or weakness, stomach pain (especially on the upper right side), nausea or vomiting, flu-like symptoms, or itching — these may be signs of a liver problem. Also call your doctor if you experience: changes in mood or behavior, depression, thoughts of self-harm, sleep problems, or if your asthma symptoms get worse. Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you have a severe asthma attack that does not improve with your rescue inhaler.
when_it_works: Zileuton starts working within a few hours of the first dose, but it may take several days to weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit in controlling your asthma symptoms. Keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel fine. It is a long-term medicine meant to prevent symptoms, not treat sudden attacks.
special_populations: Liver problems: Do NOT take zileuton if you have active liver disease or liver enzyme levels that are 3 or more times the normal limit. Your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before you start and regularly while you are on this medicine. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of zileuton in these situations is not fully established. Children: Zileuton is approved for children 12 years and older. It has not been studied in children under 12. Older adults: Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially liver-related effects.
